items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Johnny Fresco, he used to contract the Hollywood Palace show, he asked me if I wanted to become a staff member and I said I would love it.

ctx.x: Can we backtrack and little and discuss how you settled in Los Angeles and how you ended up making this your home.

When Josephine Baker first came to New York, I was playing with Buddy Rich and they hired Buddy Rich’s band to accompany her in the theatres in New York, I think it was the Strand. And she suggested that we do a little act together. So, she showed me on this little tune (sings)… it’s got a little Latin beat to it. And she says, “I want you to come down when I start singing and you make a few little notes on your horn and I’ll do a little dance to that and few little notes again..” We rehearsed it and got it down…
What year was that would you say?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: I was promised that job by Johnny Fresco, the contractor

ctx.x: The Embers. Started going to the Embers and started going to the Roundtable and, you know, I just worked all around New York with a quartet for a while, you know, after

Joe and I, we terminated our association. And then I came back out here in California in 1960 -- well, I was promised a studio job at ABC with Mitchell Ayres, the Hollywood Palace show. It went on every week. I was promised that job by Johnny Fresco, the contractor, and I told Basie I had to go back to assume, you know, my work out here, you know, and I had gotten married and my daughter was -- my wife was pregnant at the time and I told him I couldn't stay too long because I had a job to go to, which was a…
So I ended up staying there a year. Then --
